claims.statement: Luo and Wei, arXiv:2610.31456v1 [math.AP] 22 Oct 2026: Theorem 1.1 (for unit-covolume lattices, BCC is the unique minimiser of the Yukawa energy E_kappa below a unique threshold kappa* in (0, sqrt(pi)), FCC above, both at kappa*), the characterisation (1.4) of kappa* as the unique root of an integral involving D(t) = Theta(t,L_B) - Theta(t,L_F), Lemma 6.1 (D(1) = 0 and D(t) > 0 for t > 1), Lemma A.5 (A.6)-(A.8), Lemma A.6 (2(E(L_B) - E(L_F)) < -1e-19 at kappa = 1717921868469903/10^15 and > 1e-20 at ...904/10^15), Lemmas A.1-A.4, and the printed value kappa* = 1.7179218684699 (1.717921868469903 < kappa* < 1.717921868469904 in (A.9)).
Luo and Wei, Theorems 5.1 and 6.1 and the analytic reductions of Sections 2-5 (including the global comparison that Lemmas A.2-A.4 serve) are taken as stated; this paper did not check them.

kappa* reproduced three independent ways: (E) Ewald split in Arb at 320 bits: [1.717921868469903864250874 +/- 1.67e-25]; (D) direct real-space Arb sum over about 4000 shells with a rigorous integral tail: bracket [1.717921868469903864248480 +/- 2.6e-25, 1.717921868469903864252817 +/- 4.5e-25]; (Q) mpmath quadrature of the paper's integral equation (1.4) at 40 digits: 1.71792186846990386425087416661. (E) and (Q) agree to all 25 printed digits and (D)'s interval (width ~4e-24) contains both; the printed 1.71792186846990 and the (A.9) enclosure are reproduced. Independent AI audit (AUDIT.md item 3), classical eta-split Yukawa Ewald in mpmath at 70 digits (eta = 1 and 1.3 agree to < 5e-70; matches a direct sum at kappa = 6): kappa* = 1.71792186846990386425087416660628171879468538; its independent python-flint 0.9.0 ball run reproduces both Lemma A.6 signs (G(...903) = [-1.35362654688e-19 +/- 3.3e-31], G(...904) = [2.12616065470e-20 +/- 5e-33]). Ball arithmetic and quadrature are not kernel-checked.

Lemma A.6 in Arb with full Ewald sums, G = 2(E_B - E_F): G(...903e-15) = -1.35363e-19 < -1e-19 and G(...904e-15) = +2.12616e-20 > 1e-20; controls G(...902e-15) = -2.91987e-19 and G(...905e-15) = +1.77886e-19; G(1) = -1.0745e-4, G(3) = +1.5771e-4; the direct sum agrees within its balls at every kappa; dG/dkappa at kappa* is 1.56624e-4. Not in Lean (the pinned Mathlib has no erfc).

Lemma A.6 under the paper's own truncation (FCC n <= 12, BCC l <= 48) plus the printed tail 7e-21: G_trunc(903) = -1.35362683e-19, G_trunc(904) = 2.12615782e-20; slacks 2.84e-20 (lower) and 4.26e-21 (upper); the actually omitted tail is 2.83e-26, far below the printed bound.

Lemma A.5 re-run in Arb on all 1000 + 2000 cells and (A.8): no failure; minimum slacks 7.52e-4 ((A.6), j = 999), 7.65e-5 ((A.7), j = 0), (A.8) slack 0.143. The same inequalities are Tier A in YBC-A-0003..0005; the Arb run is a cross-check.

Lemma A.3 (A.4): the three exponential bounds hold by about 2e-16. The endpoints are outward-rounded: their numerators lie 4.2, 1.05 and 2.5 units of the dyadic denominator beyond the exact logarithms, in the safe direction (independent AI audit, AUDIT.md NONBLOCKING 1). For alpha_1 and alpha_2 the rationals 11/25 and 147/1000 are themselves intermediate (the proof of Prop. 3.1 has slack of about 3e-3 and 5e-4), so only the bound for beta is tight. These are the tightest margins we met in the appendix; at 320 bits all three hold, and we do not call them an error.

Shell bounds N_n < 30n for n <= 2100 and M_l < 30 l (and M_l <= 18 l) for l <= 4200 hold on the enumerated range, by brute-force enumeration of r_3 cross-checked against the r_3 shortcut. For all n the bound is a paper argument (Prop. 4.1 / fixing two coordinates); it is not machine-checked.

Lemma 6.1 itself (D(1) = 0 and D(t) > 0 for t > 1) is NOT kernel-checked. Its finite inputs are Tier A (YBC-A-0005, YBC-A-0006); the assembly (theta functions as lattice sums over Z^3, Poisson summation for D(1) = 0 using L_B = L_F^*, the cell argument for D' and D, and N_n < 30n for all n) is the paper's argument, read and followed, not formalised. mpmath gives D(1) = -8.6e-42 numerically at 40 digits.

HEADLINE. Every printed number and inequality of Luo and Wei that we checked holds, and no discrepancy was found: kappa* (three ways), the Lemma A.6 signs, Lemma A.5 (A.6)-(A.8), the shell multiplicities, the Lemma 6.1 constants and tails, Lemmas A.1 and A.3 endpoints. NOT checked: the Lemma 6.1 assembly, Lemma A.4 (5,828 rectangles; the partition data is not public, no ancillary files on arXiv), Lemma A.2, Lemma A.6 in Lean, and Sections 2-5. This is a partial independent check, not a verification of Theorem 1.1 and not a refutation. Filed C because the headline combines Tier C ball arithmetic with Tier A finite statements.

The producer's IEEE-double direct sum reproduces kappa* to 11 digits (1.7179218684625486) because of cancellation (dG/dkappa about 1.57e-4); this describes the producer's method: the audit's float64 Ewald reaches about 12 digits (errors 5e-13 to 4e-12 depending on eta), the intrinsic limit being about eps*|S|/G' ~ 1e-12. Double precision cannot resolve the 1e-15-wide enclosure (A.9), so it is not used as a control.
